chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:

Whoever feeds a hungry believer, God will feed him from the fruits of Paradise. Whoever clothes him from his nakedness, God will clothe him in brocade and silk. Whoever gives him a drink when he is thirsty, God will give him the sealed nectar to drink. And whoever assists him or alleviates his distress, God will shade him under the shade of His Throne on the Day when there is no shade except His shade.

key_terms.استبرق: Istabraq — thick brocade or heavy silk, mentioned in the Quran as garments of Paradise (18:31, 76:21)
key_terms.الرحيق المختوم: Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum — the sealed nectar, a pure drink of Paradise mentioned in Quran 83:25-26
key_terms.ثمار الجنة: Fruits of Paradise — the heavenly sustenance promised to the righteous
key_terms.عرشه: His Throne — the Throne of God, representing divine sovereignty and shelter
key_terms.مؤمنا: A believer (mu'min) — one who possesses faith (iman)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for feeding a hungry believer in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) enumerates four forms of charitable service to a fellow believer — feeding the hungry, clothing the unclothed, quenching thirst, and assisting in hardship — each with a corresponding divine reward in the Hereafter. This hadith was narrated through the Imams and highlights the reciprocal nature of divine generosity toward those who serve His creation.
